zh.title: 之九 · 心灵的眼睛就是证明
zh.deck: 量角器量的是纸上的这个三角形。证明，让心灵怎样看见？

paragraphs: 人的心灵不能随着身体被完全毁灭，它有某种东西留下来，那是永恒的。这是第五部分第二十三条命题。
证明一共三句。神里面必然有一个概念，或者说观念，表达人的身体的本质，所以它必然是属于人的心灵本质的某种东西。能用时间界定的延续，我们只在心灵表达身体的现实存在的限度内才归给它，也就是说，只在身体延续的时候。可这个东西是凭神的本质本身，以某种永恒的必然被设想的；所以，属于心灵本质的这个东西，必然是永恒的。

sections.heading: 我们感觉到，经验到
paragraphs: 附释从这个观念说起：正如前面说过的，它在永恒的相下表达身体的本质，是属于心灵本质的一个确定的思想样式，必然是永恒的。接下来是一件做不到的事：我们不可能记得我们在身体之前存在过，因为身体里不可能有这种存在的任何痕迹，永恒也不能用时间来界定，跟时间也不能有任何关系。
可是，我们仍然感觉到，经验到，我们是永恒的。
为什么说得上感觉，他随即给了两句。心灵凭理解设想的东西，它感觉得到，不下于它记得的东西。因为心灵用来看东西，观察东西的眼睛，就是证明本身。
这本书说到眼睛，一共七处。另外六处都是身体上的眼睛：有睁着眼睛做梦的人，有照在水面上，反射进我们眼里的阳光。说心灵的眼睛，只有这一处。

sections.heading: 量角器
paragraphs: 上学的时候量过三角形的内角。三个角量下来，加在一起，有时一百七十九度，有时一百八十一度；刻度对不太准，纸上的线也有粗细。后来学了证明，过一个顶点作对边的平行线。
量角器量的，是纸上这一个。

sections.heading: 时间不能界定的
paragraphs: 附释往下是一个所以：虽然我们不记得我们在身体之前存在过，我们却感觉到，我们的心灵，就它在永恒的相下包含着身体的本质而言，是永恒的，它这样的存在，不能用时间来界定，或者说，不能用延续来说明。
附释反复提到时间：一面说它不能界定永恒，一面把它能界定的延续系在身体的现实存在上。

sections.heading: 收束
paragraphs: 心灵说得上在延续，它的存在能用一段确定的时间来界定，只在它包含着身体的现实存在的限度内。同一句里，他接着说：
也只在这个限度内，它才有力量用时间去确定事物的存在，把事物当作延续着的东西来设想。

notes: 主要位置为第五部分第二十三条命题及附释。永恒在这里与时间上的延续、身体之前的个人记忆分开，不擅自改写成灵魂无限期延续。
眼睛的七处按五部分拉丁文 ocul- 词形复核。时间一词的精确分组不作为论据，保留原文真正反复区分的永恒与延续。
zh.aside: 《SAE第一批判》要给它承担的几条配一套符号写法，动手之前先钉了一句：形式化不升格地位，一条承担写成了符号，不因此多得一分成色。斯宾诺莎在附释里谈的不是写法，是心灵拿什么看：拿证明看。这是旁注，不是论证。

en.title: The Eyes of the Mind
en.deck: For Spinoza, a demonstration is not merely a record of what the mind sees. It is how the mind sees.

paragraphs: The human mind cannot be completely destroyed with the body; something of it remains eternal. That is Proposition Twenty-Three of Part V.

The demonstration moves through three sentences. In God there is necessarily a conception or idea expressing the essence of the human body, and something corresponding to it necessarily belongs to the mind’s essence. Duration measured by time is attributed to the mind only insofar as it expresses the body’s actual existence—that is, while the body endures. What is conceived through God’s essence with eternal necessity is therefore something eternal belonging to the mind.
The claim is about eternity in this account, not simply about a very long continuation of personal life.

sections.heading: We feel and experience it
paragraphs: The scholium returns to the idea that expresses the body’s essence under a form of eternity. It is a definite mode of thought belonging to the mind and is necessarily eternal.
Then comes a limit. We cannot remember having existed before the body. The body could contain no traces of that existence, and eternity cannot be defined through time or bear a temporal relation.
Nevertheless, Spinoza says, we feel and experience that we are eternal.

He explains why the language of feeling can enter here. The mind senses what it conceives through understanding no less than what it retains in memory. The eyes through which the mind sees and observes things are the demonstrations themselves.

In the linked Latin text, references to eyes occur seven times. Elsewhere they concern bodily eyes: people dreaming with their eyes open, or rays reflected from water into the eyes. Here the image is given a different task. These are the eyes of the mind.

sections.heading: The protractor
paragraphs: At school you measure the angles of a triangle. Added together they give 179 degrees, or 181. The marks are hard to align; the drawn lines have thickness.
Later you learn a proof, drawing through one vertex a line parallel to the opposite side.
The protractor measured this triangle on the paper. The proof lets you grasp a relation the imperfect measurements were trying to approach.
That makes the contrast approachable. It does not, by itself, establish Spinoza’s account of eternity.

sections.heading: What time cannot measure
paragraphs: The scholium continues with a consequence. We do not remember existing before the body, yet we experience the mind as eternal insofar as it involves the body’s essence under a form of eternity.

Existence understood in that way cannot be measured by time or explained through duration. The repeated references to time keep separating what it cannot define from what belongs to the body’s actual continuance.
This is why the account cannot simply be read as a recovered memory of an earlier life. The text itself has denied the relevant memory and the temporal measure.

sections.heading: At the end
paragraphs: The mind is said to endure, and its existence can be measured by a definite span, only insofar as it involves the body’s actual existence.
Spinoza adds that only within that limit does the mind have the power to determine things’ existence by time and conceive them as enduring.
The scholium does not merely use the word eternal. It keeps telling the reader which familiar way of imagining it will not do.

en.aside: Before supplying symbolic notation, the SAE First Critique says that formalization does not improve a commitment’s standing merely by writing it in symbols. Spinoza’s scholium is making a different claim—not about typography, but about what the mind sees through: demonstrations themselves. Both passages concern form and understanding, but they should not be made to say the same thing.
notes: Location: V.23, demonstration and scholium. Eternity is distinguished from temporal duration and from memory of an existence before the body.

The seven eye references were checked by the Latin ocul- forms across the five linked parts. The manuscript’s exact division of five references to time is replaced by the textual distinction itself; no inference of personal immortality is added.
